**Image Analysis:**

- **Affected plant part**: Stem/culm of a cereal plant (likely wheat)
- **Key visual features**:
  - Distinct elongated, elliptical lesion on the stem
  - Dark reddish-brown core/center fading to tan/straw-colored margins
  - The characteristic "eye-shaped" appearance — darker center surrounded by lighter tissue
  - Adjacent stem tissue is green (healthy) on one side and straw/bleached on the other
  - No surface pustules or powdery coating visible

**Reasoning:**

The lesion is located on the stem/culm and displays the hallmark "eye-shaped" appearance — an elliptical lesion with a dark brown necrotic center and lighter tan borders. This is the defining characteristic of **Eyespot** (*Oculimacula* spp.), a fungal foot rot disease of cereals. 

- **Stem Rust / Wheat Stem Rust**: Ruled out — no brick-red urediniospore pustules rupturing the epidermis.
- **Cephalosporium Stripe**: Ruled out — that disease causes long yellow-tan stripes running the full length of the stem, not a discrete elliptical lesion.
- **Rhizoctonia Damping-Off**: Ruled out — affects seedlings at soil level with water-soaked rotting, not discrete stem lesions.
- **Eyespot**: Matches perfectly — discrete eye-shaped lesion on the stem with dark center and tan margins, typical of Eyespot foot rot in wheat/barley.
